Along with what I would like you to hear from me I've had to include a good deal about myself so it would make sense-hope you don't mind.

Life is short. Sexual life is shorter still. Don't draw it out until there's nothing left to work with. I love easily, and I'm a philanderer, so I no longer offer complete fidelity to partners; but I am emotionally faithful, and still love and care about the women I've parted from. All of them, whether I married them or not. John Hartford, an American songwriter, has a line: "I regret my life won't be long enough, to make love with all the women that I'd like to: least of all to live with the ones I've loved." I believe that to be a truer picture of general male consciousness than other descriptions I've seen. Not saying there aren't faithful men, of course there are. But it isn't my natural state, and that changes what I think and say here. Nowadays, I suppose I would be considered polyamorous.

I'm 68, male. Two divorces. Brad has a long way to go, farther than you do. Frustrating and difficult for you, short and longer term. Even if you do end up together, there are going to be echoes that ring through your lives for a long time. That's okay, actually, nothing to keep you away.

I'd like to offer a picture that probably not everyone would approve. First, nothing should happen until Brad actually quits the house and gets a separate dwelling. Never mind the divorce filing, in itself that's not serious. You've got to see real evidence before you get closer. Get the divorce COMPLETELY out of the way, legally over. Not just separation, the final decree. You can fool around all you like, but don't move in together. Then Brad will need a period of time; three months, six months, a year...before he knows who he is again. And he may change. Sulking and introspection take their own time; nothing to be done but wait. There's a line here for me to say how long, but I'm not going to fill it in. Nobody knows; you might. He might. But don't let your life get away while you're waiting for these tickets (decree and introspection) there's an equal chance it'll come out good or bad; it's always worth the risk, even if it fails the pain is not unbearable, and life is to be lived. Seize the day!

tl,dr; He has to leave and get his own place. Then after the dust settles you can let it happen; but don't get serious until months after the final decree. Enjoy it to the full, but don't bet on eternity.

My club is an AMA sanctioned club in the state of Texas. We were founded in 1957 and are currently the oldest AMA club in Texas. We support many children related charities in our area, our biggest being the Texas lions camp for children with physical disabilities, type 1 diabetes and cancer. We donated, just this last week, our yearly donation that totaled to $40,000 between our 15 chapters.

We do group rides and meeting up depends on what is going on that month and what our members are doing. I am an officer in the founding chapter and try to meet up with my other officers or members on a weekly basis. I live around the corner from our secretary, who has been my best friend since 2nd grade, so we are out and about often.

Anyone with a 400cc and up street style motorcycle can join. We hold no requirements as to age, race, religion or otherwise. Our Sergeant at Arms came from the Legion Riders as their commander and felt that they were not what he was looking for in an MC.
